text:
ashley: quick heads-up 1: seeing a strange UX quirk in the Go generator streaming sample app. when a user cancels the context during the initial handshake, generator.Events() sometimes blocks forever.

ashley: minimal repro attached below (very condensed):
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 50*time.Millisecond)
g := client.NewGenerator(ctx, opt)
ch := g.Events()
go func() {
  for ev := range ch {
    _ = ev
  }
}()
// we return from handler immediately, timeout triggers
time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond) // allow cancel
// expect goroutine to exit, but it can hang
```

kevin: thanks. is the hang happening only when auth refresh is wired in? last week I saw a hang in a handler where token refresh goroutine used a separate ctx and never saw cancel.

ashley: good question. repro is flaky without auth flow, but reliably hangs when the auth shim runs a background refresh loop and we race-cancel during handshake.

rui: possible cause: generator.Events() returns a channel driven by a read loop that closes only after the http stream returns EOF or error. if the stream isn't closed on ctx cancel, the read loop blocks. do we call req = req.WithContext(ctx) for the http request that upgrades/starts the stream?

ashley: checked code: we use WithContext in the main path, but the auth layer wraps transport and may intercept RoundTrip; if it spawns a goroutine to refresh token and uses a derived ctx.WithCancel(context.Background()) that isn't tied to request ctx, cancellation won't propagate to RoundTrip.

kevin: quick fix options: 1) make generator implement Close() that cancels internal context and closes events channel; 2) ensure auth refresh uses errgroup.WithContext to inherit parent ctx; 3) make the stream read use a select on ctx.Done() in addition to read so it can bail early.

ashley: I prototyped option 1+3: add a Close() that cancels internal ctx (stored on generator struct) and change read loop to select on ctx.Done() before blocking read. local sampleapp no longer hangs. patch on branch gen-close-ctx-2026.

rui: good. can you paste the read-loop snippet? tiny diff helps reviewers.

ashley: sure:
```go
for {
  select {
  case <-g.ctx.Done():
    close(events)
    return
  default:
  }
  // blocking read from http stream
  tok, err := dec.ReadToken()
  if err != nil {
    close(events)
    return
  }
  events <- tok
}
```

kevin: looks good. also add explicit req = req.WithContext(g.ctx) immediately before RoundTrip to guard against earlier middleware swapping ctx.

ashley: added that too. tests: added a small e2e in sampleapp that cancels mid-handshake and asserts no goroutine with stack containing "dec.ReadToken" after cancel. it's a bit fiddly but stable locally.

devx-bot: CI triggered for gen-close-ctx-2026 (build #4410).

rui: small API note: if we add Close(), document that callers should call it when they stop consuming Events() or rely on ctx cancellation. sampleapp README update would prevent onboarding confusion.

ashley: will update README and add a short paragraph in the SDK migration guide (generator ergonomics section).

kevin: once CI passes, let's roll the change into the next patch release. flagging for eng-runtime review in PR description about http2 stream closing semantics.

ashley: thanks all 1: this should reduce a lot of the confusing "app never exits" issues reported by new users.
